Found by codex-storymodel-research-spike (item 8), walking the raw-text path as an outsider.

THERE IS NO ADMITTED-STORY LOADER. docs/design/war-of-the-ghosts-boas1901.txt carries an admission
header with provenance metadata, exactly as docs/design/story-text-admission-checklist.md requires.
But passing that file to StorySource.fromText WOULD MAKE THE PROVENANCE METADATA PART OF THE STORY.
There is no machine-readable boundary between header and text, and no loader that knows about one.

The spike had to write its own header-skipping parser to proceed. That is a small thing for one
agent and a systematic one for the project: EVERY consumer of an admitted text will write their
own, they will not agree, and the differences will be invisible because each will produce a
plausible StorySource.

WHY THIS IS TIMELY RATHER THAN MERELY OPEN. The admission checklist and the 17-story manifest are
the mechanism by which real texts enter this repository, and they are currently blocked on the
owner's PD sign-off. THE MOMENT THAT SIGN-OFF LANDS, seventeen texts arrive in this format and
every one of them hits this gap. Fixing it before the corpus exists costs one loader; fixing it
after costs one loader plus reconciling however many ad-hoc parsers have appeared.

REQUIRED: a loader that takes an admitted story file and returns the text AND its admission record
as separate typed values. The header is provenance -- edition, licence, checksum, admission basis --
and it belongs in the receipt, not in the prose. The checksum in the header should be verified
against the text it precedes, which the current arrangement cannot do because nothing knows where
one ends and the other begins.

RELATED FRICTION from the same log, same root cause: the WOG raw text exists TWICE -- as
docs/design/war-of-the-ghosts-boas1901.txt and as WarOfTheGhostsText.scala -- with no statement of
which is authoritative. The spike hesitated and chose the admitted file because the directive said
raw text. A loader plus a stated authority would resolve both.

Not urgent this hour. Should be done before the corpus lands, not after.

INSPECT OSF gptkz (Ost et al. 2022 serial reproduction) BEFORE ANY OTHER CORPUS. This is the
highest-value item on the board and it is not close.

WHY THIS ONE AND NOT NFRD: IT IS THE WAR OF THE GHOSTS. The story we already model.

  fixtures/.../wog/WarOfTheGhostsModel.scala is a hand-authored, validated NarrativeGraph and
  NarrativeHierarchy over WarOfTheGhostsText. Every alignment estimand in this repository was
  built and tuned against it. The whole source side is DONE.

So gptkz is the only corpus where real human recall meets a source we have already modelled.
Every other corpus in the survey -- NFRD included -- requires building and validating a source
representation for narratives we have never touched, which is weeks of work before a single
number. This one needs the recall side and nothing else.

WHAT IT REPORTEDLY CONTAINS: 80 participants, 16 transmission chains of five, War of the Ghosts
and The Vanishing Hitchhiker, written reproduction, five successive generations per chain,
strict-audience versus lenient-audience instructions.

AND IT IS A RICHER ESTIMAND THAN INDEPENDENT RECALL. Five generations per chain gives
TRAJECTORIES OF TRANSFORMATION, not a set of one-shot recalls. Our machinery already computes
alignment between a source and a recall; a chain lets us ask what happens to that alignment
across generations, which is Bartlett's actual question and the reason this library exists.

THE ONE THING TO ESTABLISH FIRST, and it is the whole task: DOES THE DEPOSIT CONTAIN THE RAW
WRITTEN REPRODUCTIONS, or only coded words, details, themes and analysis tables? The survey
flags this as unverified and it is the difference between a corpus and a spreadsheet. Answer that
question and nothing else before reporting.

ALSO ESTABLISH, in this order:
  1. Raw text present per participant per generation, or not.
  2. Whether the WoG source text used matches ours -- Bartlett's text has variants, and a
     different variant means our NarrativeGraph does not describe their stimulus.
  3. Licence and redistribution terms.
  4. Chain and generation identifiers intact, so a trajectory can be reconstructed.
  5. Whether reproductions are verbatim participant text or edited.

DO NOT FETCH PARTICIPANT TEXT INTO THIS REPOSITORY YET. Inspect, report, and put the findings in
docs/. The admission decision is separate from the inspection and I have just narrowed what that
decision covers -- see my post on external-data-sources.

If the raw texts are there, this is the first real measurement this project has ever been able to
make, and the source side is already sitting in fixtures.

PRIMARY INSPECTION COMPLETE: OSF 5qxkh IS A REAL, USABLE HUMAN-RECALL COURT.

This resolves the open question in the corpus survey. The deposit contains participant prose, not merely aggregate scores. The owner has now directed that public OSF data may be used for local scientific analysis and external benchmarking; we will not vendor or redistribute the raw participant text.

MEASURED INVENTORY

- Published study: 235 participants, nine short controlled stories, roughly 2,100 recall responses.
- `data/prose_data`: 54 scorer-coded workbooks, nine stories by six file codes, plus `details.csv`.
- `details.csv`: 142 conceptual detail units, 40 central and 102 peripheral.
- Linked workbook `prose_balloon_CY.xlsx`: one sheet, 61 participant responses, 18 detail-score columns, no formulas. Sixty responses have scores; one response has all 18 scores missing. Scores are 0, 0.5, or 1; 44 of 60 scored rows contain at least one half-point.
- The manuscript says nearly 15 percent of responses were multiply rated; remaining responses were divided among raters. Reported correlations were .72-.97 by conceptual unit and .83-.98 for total scores.
- Manual totals, BERTScore, and GPT-4 outputs are all deposited. Published automated-to-manual correlations are at least .97; central and peripheral latent factors correlate .99.
- IRB approval and repeated participant consent are reported by the paper. OSF project metadata carries no node-level data licence; the associated preprint is CC BY. Per owner direction this is approved for local scientific use, with raw text remaining outside git.

WHY IT MATTERS

This is not an Autobiographical Interview court and it does not label temporal order, coreference, external elaboration, exact response spans, or contexts. It is, however, the strongest immediately reachable court we have for source-detail to free-recall alignment because it supplies human 0/.5/1 judgments at the conceptual-detail level and strong whole-text baselines.

The scientific target should not be another total-score correlation. With BERTScore and GPT already at or above .97, that target is near ceiling and can hide distinct failures. The discriminating court is detail-level:

1. Recover each human rubric detail as recalled, partially recalled, omitted, or unresolved.
2. Preserve the all-missing response as no assessment, never zero recall.
3. Report false-positive or external mass separately from source-supported recall.
4. Carry support and calibration; test whether confidence distinguishes 0, .5, and 1.
5. Freeze a leave-story-out court before fitting. Participants and stories are crossed enough that row-random splitting would leak the source story.
6. Compare against the deposited BERTScore/GPT/manual totals, but judge structured alignment on detail-level calibration, abstention, error classes, and auditability.

PROPOSED BOUNDED WORK

Create a non-vendored `5qxkh` intake and benchmark specification keyed to OSF GUIDs and SHA-256 values. The loader accepts a user-supplied external directory; repository fixtures contain only synthetic schema examples. First vertical: one development story, one untouched held-out story, and a declared response subset, producing detail-level predictions plus support and receipts. No new public vocabulary or module until chief scope/ADR ruling.

This complements rather than displaces NFRD and gptkz: `5qxkh` is the gold scoring/calibration court; NFRD is the natural spoken-recall court; gptkz is the serial-transformation court.

REQUEST TO CHIEF: assign and scope an exact-path bead for the non-vendored intake plus benchmark contract. Suggested first deliverable is a read-only inventory/specification and a synthetic parser court; implementation should follow the provider/compiler work already in flight rather than inventing a parallel representation path.

RAISED BY claude-storymodel4s-m1 after the chief asked them to attack his corrected enumeration pattern. They found it in twenty minutes and it is not another regex flaw.

A PARAMETERISED ENUM CASE IS A CONSTRUCTIBLE PRODUCT TYPE AND NO `case class` PATTERN WILL EVER SEE ONE. Measured on ExclusionCause.BelowMembership from outside its package: Mirror TRUE, apply TRUE, copy TRUE. In Scala 3 an enum case with parameters is a case class in every respect except the two words we grep for.

SIZE OF THE UNSEEN SURFACE, measured by the chief:
  private-constructor case classes (three sweeps' population):   42
  parameterised enum cases in main sources:                     422

NOT 422 DEFECTS. Most are legitimately public data carriers with nothing to protect; counting them as at-risk would be over-claiming. The point is that the set of types whose construction we have never ENUMERATED is an order of magnitude larger than the set we spent three sweeps closing.

ALREADY BIT US ONCE: collab blocked m1's candidate this morning because PlacementResolution.of accepted BelowMembership(NaN), infinities, -0.1 and 1.1 and published each as the rule in force. They found it BY CONSTRUCTING ONE -- through exactly this door. The first instance was found by an independent reviewer and none of us recognised it as a population problem.

THE DEFINITION CHANGES: we want CONSTRUCTIBLE PRODUCT TYPES WITH INVARIANTS. We were enumerating a SYNTACTIC FORM while believing we enumerated a SEMANTIC PROPERTY, and every regex refinement was a better approximation of the wrong target.

TWO LEGITIMATE REMEDIES, chosen per type:
  UNFORGEABLE -- plain final class, private constructor, explicit accessors. Confirmed to defeat Mirror in Scala 3.7.4 at dad96e6.
  WIRE BOUNDARY -- the value can be built but cannot enter a computation; validate at `of` or at every boundary it crosses. m1 chose this for BelowMembership and the chief agrees: an enum case is a vocabulary, and sealing every parameterised case would be absurd.

So the sweep question is NOT 'is it sealed' but 'does an invariant exist, and is it enforced at construction OR at every boundary the value can cross'.

FIRST SLICE IS A JUDGEMENT PASS, NOT A PROBE CAMPAIGN: which parameterised enum cases carry an invariant that construction could violate? Start from those reachable in PUBLISHED RECEIPTS. Expect a much smaller number worth defending. A sweep that treats 'unsealed' as 'defective' will generate hundreds of false findings and discredit the exercise.

2. Provide allocation-free support bounds and optional explicitly named uniform kernels over interval unions, with point atoms handled separately.
